statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band after a second cash hour confirmed the opening advance was fully retraced rather than extended.
recommendation: Conditions are described as orderly two-way rotation inside a narrow band with decaying implied volatility. A narrow danger window is flagged from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covering the Friday power hour, the 20:00 UTC cash close and the 21:00 UTC Globex halt before a three-day U.S. weekend.
headline: Nasdaq-100 completes a full round trip to 29,468.83, net flat on the day inside a 0.67 percent band, with VIX easing to 14.15 and the 10-year at 4.774 percent off its 4.812 peak
body:
Two U.S. cash hours have now been observed and neither produced continuation. The Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,539.57 against a 29,482.32 previous close, rallied to a 29,655.22 high, then reversed the entire advance and traded at 29,468.83 at 15:27 UTC, down 0.05 percent on the day and close to a 29,456.85 session low. The full day range is 198 points, roughly 0.67 percent, which is a narrow band for a payrolls session. Opening-auction continuation from an already aligned regime is the specific evidence class that has preceded past mean-reversion failures, and the observed path is its opposite: a complete round trip with a deep, promptly delivered retracement.

The macro trigger remains the August Employment Situation released at 12:30 UTC. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 55,000, the unemployment rate held at 4.1 percent, average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent on the month, and July was revised up to a 21,000 gain from a previously reported 23,000 decline. Futures-implied odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15 to 16 September meeting moved to roughly 59 to 60 percent from a near coin flip. That is a genuine repricing, and its transmission has stayed orderly.

Cross-asset evidence supports the benign reading. VIX traded at 14.15, down 1.19 percent from a 14.32 close and inside a 13.80 to 14.36 range, so implied volatility decayed through the release and has not expanded since. The 10-year yield stood at 4.774 percent, up 1.2 basis points and off a 4.812 percent session high, while the 2-year at 4.38 percent was up about 5 basis points and the 30-year eased to 5.239 percent. That front-end concentration with an anchored long end is the signature of a policy-path repricing rather than a disorderly repricing of duration. West Texas Intermediate traded near 90.45 dollars, down 0.93 percent on the day though up close to 9 percent on the week under the standing Strait of Hormuz disruption, so the energy channel eased today rather than escalating.

Index and internal direction remain divergent rather than aligned. The Nasdaq-100 is essentially unchanged while the Dow is down about 0.70 percent and the S&P 500 down about 0.49 percent. Delayed shared context shows the same split inside the index: semiconductors were broadly bid in the latest session while the megacap cohort was mostly lower, with only one of eight names positive. Sharp rotation of this kind raises uncertainty and is reflected in an elevated Stress reading, but internal divergence is the opposite of the aligned one-way structure that would raise Tail. Volatility decay, an observed full retracement and unaligned cross-assets together hold Tail in the low band, one point below the previous assessment.

The remaining structure of the day is mechanical rather than macro. No further U.S. macro release is scheduled today. The U.S. cash close falls at 20:00 UTC and CME Globex equity futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend, so the final eighteen hours of the horizon carry no live price path at all. The narrow danger window from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covers the Friday power hour and the closing auction, where position adjustment before a three-day weekend concentrates into a short span. U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are the Producer Price Index on 10 September and the Consumer Price Index on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.

The principal limitation is that only two cash hours have been observed and the index is now probing the lower edge of its band. A decisive break of the 29,456 to 29,655 range accompanied by shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements would invalidate this reading, and the danger window is therefore held across the late session rather than closed on the strength of an orderly first two hours.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours divide into three phases. Through the 3 September U.S. session the assessment tracked a technology-led advance that lifted Tail into the watch band between 15:00 and 18:00 UTC as trend-up structure developed, with the Nasdaq-100 closing 1.16 percent higher at 29,482.32. Overnight the mode returned to normal and Tail fell to a trough of 12 as the advance consolidated without extension. From 04:00 UTC the scores drifted higher hour by hour as pre-payrolls positioning built, peaking at Tail 24 and Stress 76 in the 12:00 UTC slot immediately after the release, when the surprise was verified but no post-release price path was yet observable. The 13:00 and 14:00 UTC slots then eased to Tail 20 and 18 as the release spike was given back and the cash open failed to produce continuation.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits cleanly at the weekend halt. Through the remaining cash session the modelled path decays into the low band on the condition that the 29,456 to 29,655 band continues to contain trade and no repeated extension after failed retracements appears, reaching its trough around 18:00 UTC when pre-holiday midday liquidity is thinnest. A lift into the watch band is modelled for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC hours, where Friday power-hour flows, the cash close and gap risk before a three-day weekend concentrate position adjustment into a narrow span. From the 21:00 UTC CME Globex halt the final eighteen hours carry no live price path, so the modelled scores fall to a floor that reflects a closed market rather than an assessment of structure, easing to a trough overnight and then lifting marginally as the accumulated weekend headline window grows toward the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen. Confidence decays slowly throughout because Friday's verified evidence ages without replacement. Beyond the horizon, U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.

Rotation of that depth is not mean-reversion failure.
